topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture objectives, reviews the multi-step model of cancer progression, and outlines the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Proliferation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling cascades such as Wnt/beta-catenin, RTK/Ras/MAPK, and PI3K/AKT drive cell-cycle progression and growth signal independence.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic alterations that arrest terminal cell differentiation promote tumor expansion in leukemias and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how mutations disrupting p53 signaling and the balance between Bax and BCL2 allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and senescence through telomere maintenance and TERT activation, concluding the discussion of cell-intrinsic growth control mechanisms.

topics.label: Cancer Metabolism and the Warburg Effect
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metabolic rewiring of cancer cells toward aerobic glycolysis, the clinical utility of metabolic imaging, and the influence of oncometabolites on the epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the angiogenic switch, examining how tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to overcome hypoxia and obtain necessary nutrients.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Dissemination, and Genetics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the multi-step metastatic cascade, diagnostic tracking through lymph node and blood biomarkers, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Conclusion and Summary of Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing how diverse mutational paths converge on common hallmarks and previewing upcoming course activities.
